cohort: The study included 204 umbilical cord samples from cases of pregnancy loss (130 without developmental abnormalities, 62 with congenital malformations, 12 with IUGR) and 21 control samples obtained from planned caesarean sections without fetal or neonatal distress.
finding: The study found a significant reduction of umbilical cord telomere length in cases of malformations, IUGR, and spontaneous abortion, with shorter telomere length associated with the severity of malformations.
cross-section timing: Umbilical cord samples were collected at birth (for controls and cases of malformation/IUGR) or at the time of pregnancy loss (for spontaneous abortion cases).
